statement: The first line holds n; the second holds n non-negative integers. Print the maximum value of any pair's XOR. Build a bitwise trie: each number inserted as its 32 bits, highest bit first. Then for each number walk down preferring the child with the opposite of its current bit - opposite bits contribute a 1 to that position of the XOR, and a high 1 outweighs everything below it - falling back to the same bit when the opposite child is missing. Track the best result across all numbers.

example.why: 5 XOR 25 is 28: their binary rows disagree at three high positions.

hint: Insert all numbers first, then query each; the greedy is safe because high bits dominate.
mistake: Walking toward the same bit - that hunts the minimum XOR, the exact opposite errand.
